subject: chubb
note: P4's fork register for the de novo encoding of the Codex/Chubb hospitalization policy — the fixture Kant et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.17638) published as Appendix A.1 and scored nine queries against in Appendix A.2. WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL. The benchmark this replicates resolved every ambiguity in the policy SILENTLY: its ground truth is nine labels of the form `Answer: "No."`, with no clause citation, no rationale, and no record of any interpretive choice. Twenty-eight of those choices are below. TEN of them bear on at least one of the paper's nine queries, and four are outcome-determinative for a published label — F-13-PENDING-SCOPE decides query 3, F-Q4-MOMENT-UNSTATED query 4, F-Q5-ACCIDENTAL-INJURY query 5, and F-Q9-CHAPEAU-SCOPE queries 2 and 9 jointly. The other EIGHTEEN are invisible to all nine queries: no query mentions a dispute, none supplies a wellness-visit date, none sits at a deadline boundary, and none puts the premium, the term or the arbitration machinery in issue. The claim this register makes is not that the paper's answers are wrong — on eight of nine we agree with them — but that a key which records only its outputs cannot be audited, cannot be disagreed with in detail, and cannot tell a downstream user which of its labels were hard. NOTHING HERE IS MATERIALISED, AND THE REASON IS WHEN THE ENCODINGS WERE WRITTEN. R4 (R4-FORK-REPRESENTATION.md, RULED 2026-08-02) maps a materialised fork 1:1 onto a field of an `Interpretation` record threaded as an ordinary GIVEN. Neither module has such a record: both were written blind, from the policy text alone, by encoders whose brief was to encode the policy and answer nine queries and who were given no fork machinery to reach for. So 24 entries are `resolved-at-encode`, 4 are `delegated-to-fact`, and `interpretation_type` is absent because there is no type to name. That places this register beside the BNA's twelve (PR #195), which materialised none, and NOT beside the Reg CF de novo register at jl4/examples/legal/regcf/denovo/fork-register.json, which materialises SIX of its twenty-six as fields of an `Interpretation` record. VERIFIED 2026-08-31 by counting the `materialisation` values in both committed registers, because an earlier framing of this exercise asserted that no inventory anyone has produced had ever materialised a fork, and that is not so. Materialisation is a discriminator, not a default: it is what an encoder does when a fork has two live readings, an executable difference, and an encoding built to carry both. WHICH OF THESE WOULD BE MATERIALISED IN A REBUILD. Ten entries carry TWO LIVE readings — F-11-CLOCK is not among them, but F-11-PREMIUM-TIMING, F-13-PENDING-BOUNDARY, F-13-PROVENANCE, F-13-AS-AT-WHICH-EVENT, F-12-CANCELLATION-MOMENT, F-12-TERM-END, F-36-TERM-START, F-321-EXTINGUISHMENT-WINDOW, F-321-SIXTY-DAY-EXPIRY and F-31-24-HOUR are — and that is the shape R4 materialises. Eight of the ten are ones the two encodings actually split on; the other two (F-321-EXTINGUISHMENT-WINDOW, F-31-24-HOUR) have two live readings that neither encoding threads. A rebuild under R4 would put those ten on an `Interpretation` record and leave the remaining eighteen where they are. SITE PATHS point at the de novo module and use ANCHORS AND NO LINE NUMBERS, deliberately: this register was written in the same run that deposited the module, other agents were still editing it, and a line number that rots looks exactly like a line number that is right. WITNESSES MARKED 'MEASURED' were produced on 2026-08-31 by the SPEC.md §8 diff oracle (`node etc/go/lib/denovo-diff.mjs run --map jl4/examples/legal/chubb/denovo/surface-map.json`), which compared the two encodings over 11 declared pairs and 34 battery rows: 374 evaluations per side, 350 agreements, 24 divergences, 12 distinct witnesses, exit 1, every disposition UNTRIAGED. EVERY ONE OF THE TWELVE LANDS ON A FORK RECORDED HERE — F-13-PENDING-BOUNDARY (triage rows 1, 4, 5 and part of 9), F-12-TERM-END (2, 12 and part of 9), F-12-CANCELLATION-MOMENT (3 and part of 10), F-13-PROVENANCE (6, 7), F-13-AS-AT-WHICH-EVENT (8), F-36-TERM-START (10), F-11-PREMIUM-TIMING (part of 9) and F-321-SIXTY-DAY-EXPIRY (11) — so the oracle found no divergence this register cannot explain, and the register predicted every divergence the oracle found. WITNESSES NOT SO MARKED are fact patterns reasoned from the two modules' text, and each says where the instrument cannot reach them. The commonest reason is that JSONDECODE cannot supply an enum constructor, which puts the whole of clause 2.1's causal limbs and BOTH top-level payability decisions outside the comparator — measured, with the two error texts, in the surface map's note. READ THIS REGISTER AGAINST FOUNDATION.md §4.2, which is its source: 35 raw entries recorded by three blind encoders, consolidated here rather than re-derived. Where an entry cites a FOUNDATION.md item (A1-A35) or a fixture defect (D1-D20), that is the provenance of the observation, not a second authority for it. WHAT DID NOT BECOME AN ENTRY, named so nobody has to diff the two documents. A4 (is clause 1.1's numbered list definitional or merely sufficient) and A8 (one policy period or renewable ones): both encodings took the same reading and neither recorded a competing one worth executing. A6 (whose signature clause 1.1(1) tests): stipulated away by the benchmark's own prompt. A10 (does 'in a timely fashion' attach to one of clause 1.3's deadlines or both): ABSORBED — on re-reading the de novo module its satisfaction test consults BOTH deadlines, so what FOUNDATION.md saw as a one-deadline reading is the PENDENCY test, and that is carried by F-13-PENDING-SCOPE and F-13-PENDING-BOUNDARY. A18 (at which month a clause 1.2 cancelation for failure of clause 1.3 bites): absorbed into F-13-PENDING-BOUNDARY, which is where the two encodings actually differ about it. A23 (does 'arising out of' modify the event or the sickness or injury): FOUNDATION.md records that no fact pattern was found on which the two readings diverge, and none was found here either. A31 (the arbitration award as a condition precedent): both encodings gate it on a dispute having arisen and it is measured by the `award-condition-precedent` pair, with no second reading surviving. A34 (whether clause 3.3.1's choice of law is operative on payability): both took it as not operative, and it appears here as the LICENCE for a reading rather than as a fork of its own — see F-Q5-ACCIDENTAL-INJURY. A12 and A13 are folded into F-13-AS-AT-WHICH-EVENT's notes. THREE ENTRIES HERE APPEAR IN NO FOUNDATION.md ROW. F-Q4-MOMENT-UNSTATED promotes its §1.3 argument to a fork; F-13-AS-AT-WHICH-EVENT is new; and F-321-SIXTY-DAY-EXPIRY is new because no single encoder could have seen it — it takes two encodings side by side to notice that one wrote AT LEAST where the other wrote GREATER THAN. That last one is the clearest thing this exercise found that nobody had already written down, and it is an argument for the §8 oracle as a fork-FINDING instrument and not only a fork-checking one.

readings.description: Whether an injury is "accidental" is judged by whether the RESULT was unexpected, unusual and unforeseen from the insured's point of view, not by whether the act that produced it was voluntary. A deliberate stunt punch that fractures a bone is a deliberate act with an unintended injury, and so an accidental injury.

citations.cite: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.3.1: "Your Policy is governed by the laws of New York."

Miller v Continental Ins. Co., 40 NY2d 675, 358 NE2d 258 (NY Court of Appeals, 23 November 1976) (Fuchsberg J) — a self-administered drug overdose held capable of being an accidental death, the intentional act notwithstanding, applying New York's rule that no distinction is drawn between accidental means and accidental results (McGroarty v Great Am. Ins. Co., 36 NY2d 358 (1975))
Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 2.1, which enumerates skydiving, military, fire, police and age and contains NO intentionally-self-inflicted-injury exclusion

readings.description: "Accidental injury" requires accidental MEANS: an injury produced by a voluntary act is not accidental however unwelcome its consequence. On this reading a hospitalization for punching one's own face is neither a sickness nor an accidental injury, and clause 1.1's definite description does not reach it. This is the reading the published answer key takes.
readings.foreclosure: Foreclosed by the policy's own choice of law rather than by any argument against it: New York, whose law clause 3.3.1 selects, is reported to have abandoned the accidental-means/accidental-result distinction. The reading remains good law in jurisdictions that keep the distinction, it is the reading the benchmark's published label depends on, and nobody in this exercise has refuted it. VERIFICATION LEVEL, stated so it cannot be laundered: the Miller citation was checked on 2026-08-31 against secondary sources — the New York Court of Appeals opinion in RJC Realty Holding Corp v Republic Franklin Ins. Co. (2004), which cites it, and case-database summaries giving 40 NY2d 675, 358 NE2d 258, decided 23 November 1976 per Fuchsberg J. The case is real, it is a New York Court of Appeals decision, and it is cited for the proposition stated. The official reporter text has NOT been read, and Miller concerns accidental DEATH under a group policy rather than "accidental injury" in a hospitalization policy, so the extension to this clause is by analogy.

Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy, which has no definitions section at all — `grep -iE 'means|defined|definition|shall mean'` over the fixture returns no match

taken.rationale: NEITHER ENCODING DECIDES THIS, and that is the point of the three-constructor enum: `sickness`, `accidental injury`, `neither sickness nor accidental injury`. The ground arrives already construed, from whoever marshals a query into a claim record. What the register records is which construction the policy's own choice of law supports — the unintended-result one — and NOT the construction the benchmark run applied. All three blind encodings answered "No" to query 5 by marshalling the ground as `neither sickness nor accidental injury`; the counterfactual is in the same file (`Q5b claim`, identical but typed `accidental injury`, returns TRUE). So on this item the benchmark scores the MARSHALLING step, not the encoding step.

notes: FOUNDATION.md §1.4, where the adversarial audit of the answer key rated this the one published label that is NOT defensible.

The "No" can only be produced by construing an undefined term in the COVERAGE GRANT against the insured, in a document with no definitions section, while treating the absence of any self-harm exclusion from clause 2.1 as irrelevant.

The paper's own error analysis concedes the term is not defined: its best model missed query 5 in 9 of 10 trials, and it attributes the failure to identifying "whether it was sickness or accidental injury, which are addressed indirectly in the contract".

Divergence is 'none' — not because the readings agree, but because the encoding cannot tell them apart: the field arrives pre-construed, which is precisely what `delegated-to-fact` records. The oracle cannot reach it either, for an unrelated reason: JSONDECODE cannot supply an enum constructor, so the decisions that read this field are out of the surface map entirely.

notes: FOUNDATION.md §4.2 entry A9. The guarded arm's reviewing auditor called the same choice a boundary error while the other two auditors did not; the disagreement is about the reading, not about different code.

Divergence is 'unassessed' and the reason is the clock. The two readings first differ at a moment strictly between the 6th and 7th month anniversaries — after a conforming visit has become impossible and before the confirmation deadline arrives — and the benchmark's convention gives every encoding a clock whose only unit is the whole month. Neither encoding can represent that moment, so no battery row can exhibit the difference and no claim of extensional equivalence can be made either. It is a real fork that this instrument cannot measure.

This is also where fixture defect D3 lives: clause 1.1(3) is satisfied while the condition is "still pending OR … satisfied in a timely fashion", while clause 1.2 deems cancelation where it "has NOT been satisfied in a timely fashion" with no pendency carve-out. Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy, which contains no notice provision of any kind

provisions: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.2.1

source.quote: such arbitration to be commenced within three (3) months from the day such parties are unable to settle the dispute or difference. If You fail to commence arbitration in accordance with this clause, it is agreed that any cause of action and any right to make a claim that You have or may have against Us shall be extinguished completely.

citations.cite: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.2.1

readings.description: The test is whether arbitration has been commenced within the window; if it has not, the right is extinguished. The clause is read without an "as at" moment.

citations.cite: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.2.1, "If You fail to commence arbitration in accordance with this clause", which states a condition and no time at which it is assessed

readings.description: Nothing is extinguished until the three months have run: before the deadline there is no failure to commence, only a period in which commencement is still open. The limb needs the same three-valued treatment — pending, performed, breached — that clause 1.3 gets.

citations.cite: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.2.1, which grants three months and so makes commencement timely at any point inside them

Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 1.1(3), the drafter's own three-valued treatment of a deadline elsewhere in the same instrument ("still pending or has been satisfied in a timely fashion")

taken.rationale: TAKEN BY OMISSION IN BOTH ENCODINGS, and this is the most interesting agreement in the whole comparison. Neither gives the limb an as-at moment, so a claim is extinguished while the three-month window is still open. FOUNDATION.md §4.1 records that all three blind encodings made the same omission and diagnoses the cause as LEXICAL rather than logical: clause 1.3 is reached through clause 1.1(3)'s words "still pending", and every encoder built careful three-valued machinery for it; clause 3.2.1 says only "If You fail to commence", and every encoder built none. A three-valued treatment appears where the source text names the third value and not where it does not.

witnesses: MEASURED 2026-08-31: battery row `dispute, impasse in month 2, arbitration never commenced`, with the hospitalization in month 3 — one month into a three-month window that has not run out. BOTH encodings answer TRUE (extinguished) on the `arbitration-extinguished` pair, which agrees on all 34 rows. Under `extinguishedOnlyOnceTheWindowHasRun` the answer is FALSE.

AGREEMENT HERE IS EVIDENCE OF A BUG, NOT OF CORRECTNESS. The oracle's own Limits section names this failure mode — "both sides erroring identically counts as agreement" — and this is its non-erroring twin: two encodings can agree perfectly and be wrong together.
notes: FOUNDATION.md §4.2 entry A32 and §4.1. It is also threat T5 in FOUNDATION.md §5.2, demonstrated rather than argued: three encodings share a confirmed logic error and all three still score 8 of 9, because no benchmark query mentions a dispute.
It is deliberately NOT fixed here. FOUNDATION.md's open item 3 asks whether to repair it before the measurement phase or leave it in as a documented control; leaving it in is what makes it evidence.

No encoding produced under that convention can express sixty days at all, in either target language. Outside the convention L4 can: `jl4-core/libraries/daydate.l4` does month-granular calendar arithmetic with the end-of-month clamp documented and cross-validated against Excel EDATE and FEEL on Drools and Camunda.

Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 1.3 and clause 3.6, which state every other period in months and years — the mismatch is the drafter's

taken.rationale: Taken by all three blind encodings, and disclosed in each. FOUNDATION.md calls it the one genuine encoded shortcut in every file.

notes: FOUNDATION.md §4.2 entry A29.

Divergence is 'none' because the month clock cannot represent the difference: no fact either encoding accepts distinguishes 59 days from 62. The harm is currently nil for a second reason — the decision that consumes the constant is deliberately not wired into payability. See F-321-SIXTY-DAY-BAR.

readings.description: A bar on recovering on the policy is a bar on the policy responding, so it is one more thing that must be true before a benefit is payable.
readings.rejection_rationale: The drafter used "condition precedent to our liability" in the sentence immediately before this one and did not use it here, which is about as clear an internal signal as an instrument gives. Folding it in would turn "not yet enforceable" into "not covered" for every claim in its first two months.

citations.cite: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.2.1, read as a single set of conditions on liability

taken.rationale: Taken by both encodings, and both keep the decision OUT of the top-level payability test while still exposing it as a named answer — so a reviewer can see the clause was read and see that it was not allowed to defeat cover.

witnesses: Battery rows `recovery sought one month after written proof of claim` and `recovery sought with no written proof of claim submitted`: MEASURED 2026-08-31, both encodings answer FALSE on the `sixty-day-bar` pair and neither lets that answer reach payability. Under `furtherConditionPrecedentToLiability` those same rows would defeat the claim. The divergence between the readings is therefore in WHICH DECISION CONSUMES THE ANSWER, and no value of any fact exhibits it — which is why the pair agrees on all 34 rows and why the fork has to be written down rather than measured.
notes: FOUNDATION.md §4.2 entry A30.

Kind is `encoding-placement`: both encodings read the words the same way and differ from the rejected reading only in what the answer is wired to. That is the BNA A12 shape, and a wording-only schema would have had nowhere to put it.

provisions: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.1.1

source.quote: 3.1.1 Your Policy insures You twenty-four (24) hours a day anywhere in the world.

citations.cite: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.1.1

readings.description: The clause forecloses any territorial or time-of-day limitation, so no fact about place or hour can change any answer. Recording one would misrepresent the policy as having a limit it disclaims, and encoding a constant-TRUE conjunct puts dead weight into every downstream projection.

citations.cite: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.1.1, which imposes no condition and removes two
Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy, which contains no other territorial or temporal limitation for 3.1.1 to be read against

readings.description: The clause is operative, negatively, and is encoded as a limb of the top-level decision that is always satisfied — so that a reviewer can tell "considered and inert" from "missed".

citations.cite: Codex Insurance Limited hospitalization policy clause 3.1.1, the only affirmative statement in the instrument that the policy does anything

taken.rationale: Taken by the de novo, with a comment explaining why its `Claim` has no territory or hour field. The corpus takes the other reading and carries `3.1.1 — the Policy insures You twenty-four hours a day anywhere in the world` as a constant-TRUE limb of its top-level decision. All three reviewing auditors flagged the constant-TRUE conjunct as dead weight that shows up in any call-graph, ladder or DMN projection; the defence is that silently dropping it leaves a reviewer unable to tell a clause that was considered from one that was missed.

notes: FOUNDATION.md §4.2 entry A26.

Divergence is 'none' — the limb is constant TRUE on either reading and no fact can move it. What the fork costs is not an answer but a PAIR: because one encoding has a rule here and the other has a comment, the surface map could declare no pairing for clause 3.1.1, and the oracle refuses a call the named module does not declare.

Fixture defect D11 sits underneath: clause 3.1.1 grants cover unqualified, with no "subject to the terms, conditions and exclusions" saver, so on its face it conflicts with clause 2.1. Both encodings read it as inert rather than as overriding, and neither registers that as a fork.
